'''Revolut Group Holdings Ltd''', known as '''Revolut''',<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 June 2022 |title=Who Owns Revolut |url=https://thebanks.eu/articles/who-owns-Revolut |access-date=2024-12-21 |website=TheBanks.eu |language=en}}</ref> is a British global [[financial technology]] company headquartered in London and founded in July 2015 by [[Nik Storonsky]] and [[Vlad Yatsenko]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Browne |first=Ryan |date=2024-06-13 |title=Revolut moves global HQ to heart of London's financial district as it awaits UK bank license |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2024/06/13/revolut-moves-global-hq-in-canary-wharf-as-it-awaits-uk-bank-license.html |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref> The company offers free and [[Subscription business model|subscription‑based]] [[digital banking]] services, primarily through a mobile app.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2019-04-01 |title=What is Revolut? |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/business-47768661 |access-date=2026-05-30 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=1 February 2022 |title=Revolut to start offering loans and credit cards |url=https://www.bonkers.ie/blog/banking/revolut-to-start-offering-loans-and-credit-cards/ |access-date=2024-12-21 |website=bonkers.ie |language=en}}</ref>

== History ==
=== Early history (2015–2017) ===
Revolut was founded in 2015 by [[Nik Storonsky]] and [[Vlad Yatsenko]] as an app enabling individuals in the United Kingdom and [[European Economic Area|European Economic Area (EEA)]] to spend money abroad using [[Interbank foreign exchange market|interbank foreign exchange]] rates.<ref name="CE">{{Cite news |last=Meyer |first=Harriet |date=12 May 2016 |title=The smartphone app revolutionising foreign currency exchange |url=https://www.theguardian.com/small-business-network/2016/may/12/the-smartphone-app-revolutionising-foreign-currency-exchange |access-date=2024-03-04 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref name="founded">{{Cite web |date=16 July 2021 |title=Vlad Yatsenko, a Ukrainian who co-founded Revolut, becomes a billionaire after an $800M round and a $33B valuation |url=https://ain.ua/en/2021/07/16/revolut-raises-800m-at-33b-valuation/ |access-date=2021-07-27 |website=AIN.UA |language=en-US |archive-date=2021-07-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727154939/https://ain.ua/en/2021/07/16/revolut-raises-800m-at-33b-valuation/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Customers could use their Revolut card in 90 currencies.<ref name="CE"/><ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams-Grut |first=Oscar |title=London fintech startup Revolut is raising £10 million and signing 1,500 new customers a day |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/revolut-raising-series-a-new-customer-sign-ups-2016-4 |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=Business Insider |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2016, the company reached around 300,000 users, processing almost £1 billion in transactions.<ref name=forbes_20160725_popular>{{Cite web |last=Dawson |first=Freddie |title=Popular Revolut: Financial Disruptor Equity Raise Oversubscribed By £17m |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/freddiedawson/2016/07/25/popular-revolut-financial-disruptor-equity-raise-oversubscribed-by-17m/ |access-date=2024-04-01 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref>

Revolut then launched a [[Subscription business model|subscription-based]] app in June 2017 available to businesses across the UK and Europe. Under the name of "Revolut Business", businesses could create an account with a multi-currency [[IBAN]] to hold, exchange, and transfer money with 25 currencies.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ainger |first=Neil |date=13 June 2017 |title=Revolut expands into business market |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2017/06/13/revolut-expands-into-business-market.html |access-date=2024-04-02 |publisher=CNBC |language=en}}</ref><ref name=techcrunch_20170613_revolut>{{Cite web |last=O'Hear |first=Steve |date=13 June 2017 |title=Revolut launches business accounts in U.K. and Europe |url=https://techcrunch.com/2017/06/13/revolut-launches-business-accounts/ |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== EU banking licence and international expansion (2017–2022) ===
[[File:Vilnius Quadrum.jpg|thumb|Quadrum office complex in Vilnius, head office of Revolut Bank UAB (name visible on left)]]

It first applied for an EU banking licence in November 2017, at which time it also started work on its own [[payment processor]].<ref name="independent_8043306">{{Cite news |title=This app-only bank is the latest UK fintech firm looking to win over customers |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/indyventure/revolut-uk-fintech-european-banking-licence-apply-brexit-leave-eu-a8043306.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240209131150/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/indyventure/revolut-uk-fintech-european-banking-licence-apply-brexit-leave-eu-a8043306.html |archive-date=2024-02-09  |access-date=2024-12-23 |work=The Independent |language=en-GB |url-status=live |last=Emma|first=Rumney|date=2017-11-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=8 November 2017 |title=Revolut applies for European banking licence |url=https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/31301/revolut-applies-for-european-banking-licence |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=Finextra Research |language=en}}</ref> The bank then received its EU banking licence as well as an [[Electronic Money Institution|EMI]] licence in December 2018 from the [[European Central Bank]], facilitated by the [[Bank of Lithuania]]. Under its new license, the bank could accept deposits and offer consumer credits, but it was not allowed to provide investment services until later.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.lb.lt/en/news/revolut-granted-specialised-bank-and-electronic-money-institution-licences |title=Revolut granted specialised bank and electronic money institution licences |date=13 December 2018 |website=[[Bank of Lithuania]] |language=en |access-date=2018-12-13 |archive-date=2019-04-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190422135822/https://www.lb.lt/en/news/revolut-granted-specialised-bank-and-electronic-money-institution-licences |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=ft_989904>{{Cite web |last=Megaw |first=Nicholas |date=13 December 2018 |title=Lithuania licence lets Revolut launch banking products |url=https://www.ft.com/content/989904f0-fe2c-11e8-aebf-99e208d3e521 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181213131030/https://www.ft.com/content/989904f0-fe2c-11e8-aebf-99e208d3e521 |archive-date=2018-12-13 |access-date=2018-12-13 |website=[[Financial Times]] |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=cnbc_20181213_revolut>{{Cite web |last=Schulze |first=Elizabeth |date=13 December 2018 |title=UK fintech unicorn Revolut granted European banking license |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2018/12/13/revolut-secures-european-banking-license.html |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref>

Following the acquisition of a banking licence, the company announced plans in September 2019 for expansion into 24 new markets, supported by agreements with [[Visa Inc.|Visa]] and [[Mastercard]]. The company said that it also wanted to hire an additional 3,500 employees.<ref>{{Cite news |last=White |first=Lawrence |title=Exclusive: Fintech firm Revolut to hire 3500 staff in global push with Visa |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-revolut-visa-exclusive/exclusive-fintech-firm-revolut-to-hire-3500-staff-in-global-push-with-visa-idUSKBN1WF0JQ/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230120212955/http://www.reuters.com/article/us-revolut-visa-exclusive/exclusive-fintech-firm-revolut-to-hire-3500-staff-in-global-push-with-visa-idUSKBN1WF0JQ |archive-date=2023-01-20  |access-date=2024-12-23 |work=U.S. |language=en-US |url-status=live |date=2019-09-30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Browne |first=Ryan |date=22 October 2019 |title=Revolut strikes deal with Mastercard to accelerate expansion into the US |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2019/10/22/revolut-partners-with-mastercard-to-accelerate-us-expansion.html |access-date=2024-03-12 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.siliconrepublic.com/companies/revolut-visa-deal-fintech-markets |title=New deal with Visa will see Revolut hire thousands, expand into 24 markets |last=Short |first=Eva |date=30 September 2019 |website=Silicon Republic |language=en |access-date=2019-10-07 |archive-date=2021-03-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210310173503/https://www.siliconrepublic.com/companies/revolut-visa-deal-fintech-markets |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2019, the Revolut app launched in beta to the Australia region.<ref name=techcrunch_20190612_revolut>{{Cite web |last=Dillet |first=Romain |date=13 June 2019 |title=Revolut launches in Australia as a beta release |url=https://techcrunch.com/2019/06/12/revolut-launches-in-australia-as-a-beta/ |access-date=2024-08-26 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref> The following month, Revolut expanded to Singapore.<ref name=techcrunch_20191023_revolut>{{Cite web |last=Dillet |first=Romain |date=23 October 2019 |title=Revolut launches publicly in Singapore, signs deal with Mastercard |url=https://techcrunch.com/2019/10/23/revolut-launches-publicly-in-singapore-signs-deal-with-mastercard/ |access-date=2024-04-04 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2020, the app launched in the United States and Japan.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Revolut launches its financial app in Japan |url=https://techcrunch.com/2020/09/07/revolut-launches-its-financial-app-in-japan/ |access-date=2020-09-08 |website=[[TechCrunch]] |date=7 September 2020 |language=en-US |archive-date=2021-07-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210715163511/https://techcrunch.com/2020/09/07/revolut-launches-its-financial-app-in-japan/ |url-status=live|last=Romain|first=Dillet}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dillet |first=Romain |date=2020-03-24 |title=Revolut launches its neobank in the US |url=https://techcrunch.com/2020/03/24/revolut-launches-its-neobank-in-the-us/ |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref>

By November 2020, Revolut reported that it had reached breakeven. At that time, it was valued at £4.2 billion.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Browne |first=Ryan |date=8 December 2020 |title=Revolut, Europe's $5.5 billion digital bank, quietly broke even in November |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2020/12/08/digital-bank-revolut-breaks-even-in-november.html |access-date=2020-12-11 |website=[[CNBC]] |language=en |archive-date=2021-05-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210523123751/https://www.cnbc.com/2020/12/08/digital-bank-revolut-breaks-even-in-november.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

The company applied for banking licence in the United Kingdom and a bank charter in the United States in early 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-01-11/revolut-applies-for-u-k-banking-license-in-search-for-expansion |title=Revolut Applies for U.K. Banking License |newspaper=Bloomberg |date=11 January 2021 |via=www.bloomberg.com |access-date=2021-01-13 |archive-date=2021-02-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206172226/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-01-11/revolut-applies-for-u-k-banking-license-in-search-for-expansion |url-status=live |last=Stefania|first=Spezzati}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/business/financial-services/challenger-bank-revolut-bids-to-take-on-high-street-b828025.html |title=Challenger bank Revolut bids to take on high street |date=11 January 2021 |website=www.standard.co.uk |access-date=2021-01-13 |archive-date=2021-02-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210218091857/https://www.standard.co.uk/business/financial-services/challenger-bank-revolut-bids-to-take-on-high-street-b828025.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="dillet">{{Cite web |url=https://techcrunch.com/2021/03/22/revolut-applies-for-bank-charter-in-the-us/ |title=Revolut applies for bank charter in the US |date=22 March 2021 |website=[[TechCrunch]] |language=en-US |access-date=2021-04-14 |archive-date=2021-08-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210804173617/https://techcrunch.com/2021/03/22/revolut-applies-for-bank-charter-in-the-us/ |url-status=live|last=Romain|first=Dillet}}</ref> The European Central Bank also granted Revolut a full banking licence later that year.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-12-22 |title=Revolut Bank granted full banking licence in Lithuania by ECB |url=https://internationalfinance.com/banking/revolut-bank-granted-full-banking-licence-lithuania-ecb/ |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=International Finance |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== Transition to a licensed bank (2022–2023) ===
After having secured bank licences, Revolut started moving away from being an e-money institution to a bank. In January 2022, it started operating as a bank in 10 European countries.<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 January 2022 |title=Revolut launches as a bank in 10 Western European countries |url=https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/39492/revolut-launches-as-a-bank-in-10-western-european-countries |access-date=2022-01-16 |website=Finextra Research |language=en |archive-date=2022-01-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220113092411/https://www.finextra.com//newsarticle/39492/revolut-launches-as-a-bank-in-10-western-european-countries |url-status=live }}</ref> In January 2023, the company announced that it would transfer its 2 million Irish customers to a new Irish branch, moving them from a Lithuanian [[IBAN]] to an Irish IBAN.<ref name="independent_42306631">{{Cite web |last=Weston |first=Charlie |date=23 January 2023 |title=Revolut granted Irish IBANs, piling pressure on mainstream banks |url=https://m.independent.ie/business/personal-finance/banking/revolut-granted-irish-ibans-piling-pressure-on-mainstream-banks-42306631.html |access-date=2023-01-23 |website=Irish Independent |language=en}}</ref> This was followed by a launch for IBANs in France, Netherlands and Spain in September 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Civieta |first=Óscar F. |date=13 September 2023 |title=Revolut alcanza los 2 millones de clientes en España y comienza a ofrecer IBAN local |url=https://www.businessinsider.es/revolut-alcanza-2-millones-clientes-espana-ofrece-iban-local-1304408 |access-date=2024-04-10 |website=Business Insider España |language=es}}</ref><ref name="Financial Times">{{Cite news |date=27 September 2022 |title=Revolut receives green light to run UK cryptocurrency business |url=https://www.ft.com/content/2fe924e8-1fc2-4f98-9c3f-b0eff70b2174 |access-date=2023-02-21 |work=Financial Times}}</ref> By the end of the year, it was reported that Revolut held £15.1 billion in customer deposits.<ref name="bbc_57854969">{{Cite news |date=15 July 2021 |title=Revolut becomes most valuable UK start-up after £24bn valuation |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/business-57854969 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210722003529/https://www.bbc.com/news/business-57854969 |archive-date=2021-07-22 |access-date=2021-07-16 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name="$33 billion">{{cite news |last1=Metcalf |first1=Tom |last2=Spezzati |first2=Stefania |date=15 July 2021 |title=Revolut Draws SoftBank Investment to Hit $33 Billion Value |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-07-15/revolut-draws-softbank-investment-to-hit-33-billion-valuation |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210726132305/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-07-15/revolut-draws-softbank-investment-to-hit-33-billion-valuation |archive-date=2021-07-26 |access-date=2021-08-07 |work=[[Bloomberg News]]}}</ref>

Revolut expanded its investment offerings during this time. In September 2022, the UK's [[Financial Conduct Authority]] added Revolut to its list of companies authorised to offer cryptocurrency products and services, formalising its pre-2022 unregulated crypto trading.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Revolut receives green light to run UK cryptocurrency business|url=https://www.ft.com/content/2fe924e8-1fc2-4f98-9c3f-b0eff70b2174 |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=www.ft.com}}</ref> The bank also began allowing staking for holders of [[proof of stake]] cryptocurrencies in the UK and EEA.<ref name="Financial Times" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Howcroft |first=Elizabeth |date=7 February 2023 |title=Revolut to offer returns on crypto holdings via 'staking' |url=https://www.reuters.com/technology/revolut-offer-returns-crypto-holdings-via-staking-2023-02-07/ |access-date=2023-02-21 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref> In October 2023, Revolut expanded its stock trading services to include European stock trading in the EEA.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=24 October 2023 |title=Revolut adds European listed stocks to trading platform |url=https://www.rte.ie/news/business/2023/1024/1412622-revolut-adds-european-stocks/ |journal=RTE |language=en |access-date=2024-10-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=ALLEN |first=LORCAN |title=Revolut expands share trading offering with addition of 70 European listed companies |url=https://www.businesspost.ie/news/revolut-expands-share-trading-offering-with-addition-of-70-european-listed-companies/ |access-date=2024-10-17 |website=www.businesspost.ie |language=en-US}}</ref>

In September 2022, Revolut was the target of a cyber attack that exposed the personal data of over 50,000 customers.<ref name="techcrunch_20220920_revolut">{{Cite web |last=Page |first=Carly |date=20 September 2022 |title=Revolut confirms cyberattack exposed personal data of tens of thousands of users |url=https://techcrunch.com/2022/09/20/revolut-cyberattack-thousands-exposed/ |access-date=2024-03-27 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Revolut hack exposes data of 50,000 users, fuels new phishing wave |url=https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/revolut-hack-exposes-data-of-50-000-users-fuels-new-phishing-wave/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220922094151/https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/revolut-hack-exposes-data-of-50-000-users-fuels-new-phishing-wave/ |archive-date=2022-09-22 |access-date=2022-09-22|date=2022-09-19|last=Bill|first=Toulas}}</ref> Additionally, in July 2023, a flaw in its US payment system led to the loss of $20 million in corporate funds to criminal groups between late 2021 and early 2022, though some of the money was later recouped.<ref name="AT">{{cite news |last1=Venkataramakrishnan |first1=Siddharth |last2=Quinio |first2=Akila |date=9 July 2023 |title=Revolut's US payment flaws allowed thieves to steal $20mn |url=https://www.ft.com/content/0025347f-6e0c-4dbd-9762-e4eec0431050 |work=[[Financial Times]]|access-date=2026-05-31}}</ref> On the regulatory front, Revolut halted [[cryptocurrency]] trading services for its US customers in 2023, citing the "evolving regulatory environment" as the [[United States Securities and Exchange Commission|Securities and Exchange Commission]] intensified scrutiny against the sector.<ref>{{cite web |date=4 August 2023 |title=Revolut Pulls the Plug on Crypto in US, Citing Regulatory Environment |url=https://www.financemagnates.com/cryptocurrency/revolut-ends-crypto-services-in-us-blames-regulatory-uncertainty/|access-date=2026-05-31}}</ref> Financially, despite its growth, the company reported £25m loss in 2022 amid ongoing uncertainty regarding the UK banking licence.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Makortoff |first=Kalyeena |date=2023-12-22 |title=Fintech firm Revolut hit by £25m loss after hiring spree |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2023/dec/22/fintech-firm-revolut-hit-by-25m-loss-after-rise-in-staff-wages |access-date=2026-05-30 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

=== UK banking licence and global expansion (2024–2026) ===
Revolut was also granted a British banking licence the following month, though with restrictions via the standard "mobilization" stage.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Makortoff |first=Kalyeena |date=25 July 2024 |title=Revolut finally receives UK banking licence after three-year wait |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/article/2024/jul/25/revolut-receives-uk-banking-licence-after-three-year-wait |access-date=2024-07-29 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> By the end of 2024, Revolut reported having 50 million registered users globally.<ref>{{Cite web |last=jhaxell |date=19 November 2024 |title=Revolut surpasses 50 million global customers, aims for 100m milestone |url=https://fintech.global/2024/11/19/revolut-surpasses-50m-global-customers-aims-for-100m-milestone/ |access-date=2024-11-20 |website=FinTech Global |language=en-GB}}</ref> 

In April 2025, Revolut obtained the Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPIs) licence from the [[Reserve Bank of India]] (RBI), to offer payment solutions including pre-paid cards.<ref name=indiatimes_120044076>{{Cite news |date=7 April 2025 |title=Revolut gets RBI nod for PPIs, wallets |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/technology/revolut-gets-rbi-nod-for-ppis-wallets/articleshow/120044076.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-06-20 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

In May 2025, Revolut announced that it plans to invest $1.1 billion over the next three years to expand in France and made Paris its Western European headquarters, at the {{Interlanguage link|Choose France|fr}} summit.<ref name=co_20250519_revolut>{{Cite news |last=Warrington |first=James |date=19 May 2025 |title=London fintech giant piles £840m into France after criticising UK |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2025/05/19/revolut-snubs-britain-for-france-with-850m-investment/ |access-date=2025-05-20 |work=The Telegraph |language=en-GB |issn=0307-1235}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Howcroft |first=Elizabeth |date=19 May 2025 |title=Revolut plans $1.1 billion French expansion |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/revolut-plans-11-billion-french-expansion-will-apply-banking-licence-2025-05-19/ |publisher=Reuters|access-date=2026-05-31}}</ref>  

In June 2025, Revolut announced its plans to acquire {{Interlanguage link|Cetelem Argentina|es}}, an Argentina-based lender, from [[BNP Paribas]]. Terms were not disclosed.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Madry |first=Kylie |last2=Madry |first2=Kylie |date=2025-06-26 |title=Revolut to acquire BNP Paribas-owned Argentine lender in market expansion |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/revolut-acquire-bnp-paribas-owned-argentine-lender-market-expansion-2025-06-26/ |access-date=2025-08-05 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref> The same month, Béatrice Cossa-Dumurgier (a former board member of [[Société Générale]] and executive at BNP Paribas) was appointed CEO of Revolut's Western Europe headquarters, based in Paris.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.globalwomanleader.com/news/revolut-appoints-beatrice-cossa-dumurgier-as-ceo-of-western-europe-hq-in-paris-nwid-4457.html|title=Revolut Appoints Beatrice Cossa-Dumurgier as CEO of Western Europe HQ in Paris|access-date=2026-05-31}}</ref> In September 2025, it named former [[Société Générale]] CEO [[Frédéric Oudéa]] as Chairman of its Western Europe hub.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Howcroft |first=Elizabeth |last2=Rosemain |first2=Mathieu |last3=Howcroft |first3=Elizabeth |last4=Rosemain |first4=Mathieu |date=2025-09-05 |title=Revolut hires former SocGen boss Oudea as West Europe chairman |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/revolut-hires-former-socgen-boss-oudea-west-europe-chairman-2025-09-05/ |access-date=2025-09-11 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref>

=== US expansion (2025–2026) ===
In 2025, Revolut explored an existing US bank acquisition to further expand its global footprint.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/revolut-weighs-buying-us-bank-global-expansion-push-executive-says-2025-09-23/|title=Revolut weighs buying US bank in global expansion push, executive says|last=Reggiori Wilkes|first=Tommy|date=23 Sep 2025|access-date=1 February 2026|work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> In February 2026, the company announced that it was shifting its plan to establish an independent national charter and had applied for a license with the [[Office of the Comptroller of the Currency]] (OCC).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/christerholloman/2026/02/01/why-revolut-pivots-to-standalone-us-bank-license-strategy/|title=Why Revolut Pivots To Standalone US Bank License Strategy|date=1 February 2026|access-date=1 February 2026|website=[[Reuters]]|last=Holloman|first=Christer|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260518190137/https://www.forbes.com/sites/christerholloman/2026/02/01/why-revolut-is-pivoting-to-a-standalone-us-bank-license-strategy/|archive-date=18 May 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=ref1/>

On 5 March 2026, Revolut announced it had applied for a US banking license with the OCC and the [[Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation|FDIC]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Revolut applies for US banking licence in push to crack American market|url=https://www.ft.com/content/86e56dad-d528-4477-a166-65607e91dc9f |access-date=2026-03-18 |website=www.ft.com}}</ref><ref name="ref1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/ronshevlin/2026/03/24/what-revolut-needs-to-do-to-succeed-in-the-us/?ss=fintech|title=Revolut: The Fintech’s Blueprint For Success In The United States|last=Shevlin|first=Ron|date=24 March 2026|website=Forbes|access-date=2026-05-31}}</ref>

In an 20 April 2026 interview to [[Bloomberg News|Bloomberg]], Revolut CEO [[Nik Storonsky]] stated that the digital bank is approximately two years away from an [[Initial public offering|IPO]], with a U.S. listing as the preference.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gani |first=Aisha S |date=20 April 2026 |title=Revolut CEO Storonsky Says Digital Bank’s IPO Is Two Years Out |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-04-20/revolut-ceo-storonsky-says-digital-bank-s-ipo-is-two-years-out |work=Bloomberg|access-date=2026-05-31}}</ref> The following day, the ''[[Financial Times]]'' reported that Revolut was targeting a market capitalisation of between $150 billion and $200 billion in its eventual IPO, and planned a secondary share sale in the second half of 2026 at a valuation exceeding $100 billion.<ref name="tc_ipo_2026">{{Cite news |last=Iyer |first=Ram |date=21 April 2026 |title=Revolut eyes valuation of up to $200B in eventual IPO |url=https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/21/revolut-eyes-valuation-of-up-to-200b-in-eventual-ipo/ |work=TechCrunch|access-date=2026-05-31}}</ref> Revolut reported revenue of $6 billion for the financial year ended 31 December 2025, up from $4 billion in 2024, and net profit of $1.7 billion, up from $1 billion, with 68.3 million retail customers at year-end.<ref name="tc_ipo_2026" />

== Products and services ==
Revolut began as a mobile app linked to a prepaid card for spending abroad and foreign exchange.<ref name="GuardianFX2016">{{cite news |last=Meyer |first=Harriet |date=12 May 2016 |title=The smartphone app revolutionising foreign currency exchange |url=https://www.theguardian.com/small-business-network/2016/may/12/the-smartphone-app-revolutionising-foreign-currency-exchange |access-date=9 July 2026 |work=The Guardian}}</ref> The company later expanded into banking, business accounts, lending, subscriptions, investments and cryptocurrency services.<ref name="ReutersProfit2025">{{cite news |date=24 April 2025 |title=Revolut profit soars to record $1.5 billion as Storonsky increases stake to more than 25% |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/revolut-profit-soars-15-billion-storonsky-increases-stake-more-than-25-2025-04-24/ |access-date=9 July 2026 |work=Reuters}}</ref>

Revolut expanded into investing in 2019 and launched in-app share trading for European customers. ''Wired'' reported that the service allowed trading in 300 US-listed stocks on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq.<ref name="WiredTrading2019">{{cite news |date=1 August 2019 |title=Revolut's adding stock trading to its app to get millennials investing |url=https://www.wired.com/story/revolut-trading-stocks-shares-app |access-date=9 July 2026 |work=Wired}}</ref> After receiving a UK trading licence in 2024, Revolut expanded its investment offering to include UK and EU-listed stocks and ETFs, and later launched a UK stocks and shares ISA using ETFs from providers including BlackRock and Vanguard.<ref>{{cite news |date=18 November 2024 |title=Revolut gets UK trading license, set to offer UK & EU stock trading |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/revolut-gets-uk-trading-license-set-offer-uk-eu-stock-trading-2024-11-18/ |access-date=9 July 2026 |work=Reuters}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=8 July 2025 |title=Revolut launches its first stocks and shares ISA with BlackRock and Vanguard ETFs |url=https://moneyweek.com/personal-finance/isas/revolut-launches-stocks-and-shares-isa |access-date=9 July 2026 |work=MoneyWeek}}</ref>

==Criticism and controversies==
Revolut has been subject to criticism and many controversies, such as issues with customer support and long-lasting lockouts,<ref>{{Cite news |first1=Laura |last1=Noonan |first2=Siddharth |last2=Venkataramakrishnan |first3=Ella |last3=Hollowood |date=6 April 2023 |title=Fintechs face reckoning over customer service |url=https://www.ft.com/content/da82bae4-5846-499d-9a9e-f6a429fa9528 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241120014554/https://www.ft.com/content/da82bae4-5846-499d-9a9e-f6a429fa9528 |archive-date=2024-11-20 |access-date=2024-12-21 |work=Financial Times}}</ref> as well as [[anti–money laundering]] compliance failures<ref>{{Cite web |first=Shruti |last=Khairnar |date=2 October 2023 |title=Revolut reportedly in talks with the UK's FCA over AML failures |url=https://www.fintechfutures.com/aml-solutions/revolut-reportedly-in-talks-with-the-uk-s-fca-over-aml-failures |access-date=2024-12-21 |website=www.fintechfutures.com |language=en-GB}}</ref> and lack of support for [[Defrauder|defrauded]] customers.<ref name=theguardian_2024apr10_im>{{Cite news |last=Brignall |first=Miles |date=10 April 2024 |title=I'm a victim of scammers. But Revolut says 'no' to a refund |url=https://www.theguardian.com/money/2024/apr/10/im-a-victim-of-scammers-but-revolut-says-no-to-a-refund |access-date=2024-12-21 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-14 |title=Revolut customers say e-money firm failed them after being scammed |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cj6epzxdd77o |access-date=2026-05-30 |website=www.bbc.com |language=en-GB}}</ref>

===Employment practices===
In March 2019, [[Wired (magazine)|''Wired'']] published an exposé of the company's employment practices and work culture. It included allegations by some former employees of unpaid work, high staff turnover, and employees feeling the need to work weekends to meet [[performance indicator]]s.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Mellino |first=Emiliano |date=28 February 2019 |title=Revolut insiders reveal the human cost of a fintech unicorn's wild rise |url=https://www.wired.co.uk/article/revolut-trade-unions-labour-fintech-politics-storonsky |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210901154118/https://www.wired.co.uk/article/revolut-trade-unions-labour-fintech-politics-storonsky |archive-date=2021-09-01 |access-date=2019-03-01 |magazine=Wired |language=en-UK}}</ref> A later article in December 2019 by ''Sifted'' noted that Revolut had a higher rating on [[Glassdoor]] than its peers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 December 2019 |title=Digital banks Monzo, Revolut, Starling and N26 compared |url=https://sifted.eu/articles/challenger-banks-monzo-starling-revolut-n26-compared/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191023200733/https://sifted.eu/articles/challenger-banks-monzo-starling-revolut-n26-compared/ |archive-date=2019-10-23 |access-date=2019-12-20 |website=Sifted |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== Inadequate compliance ===

In 2016, a former employee approached UK's [[Financial Conduct Authority]] with claims regarding Revolut's leadership conduct and compliance practices. The [[whistleblower]] emphasized that the company's anti-money laundering systems were utterly inadequate and that  money-laundering checks were not being properly applied for select customers. Numerous Revolut's employees contacted by [[BBC]] corroborated the whistleblower's testimony and also confirmed that Revolut's CEO allegedly ignored recommendations from its compliance team and conflicted with compliance executives. One such internal conflict led to departure of two chief risk officers, two money laundering reporting officers, a chief compliance officer, and  a chief finance officer, among other roles, within three years.<ref name=bbccompliance>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-47751945 |title=Revolut whistleblower had concerns over CEO conduct and compliance |author=Joe Witwell, Rory Cellan-Jones |date=2 April 2019 |publisher=BBC |accessdate=15 June 2026}}</ref>

In 2018, [[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]] reported that in the Summer 2018 Revolut disabled its system designed to automatically halt transactions to sanctioned individuals. In a draft letter to FCA, which was leaked to journalists, Revolut's lawyers confirmed that the internal system was changed so the transactions that potentially matched against sanctions lists were not halted, but rather flagged for inspections. The industry expert commenting on the case for BBC report emphasized that failing to halt transactions is by far the most serious compliance failure, as checking afterwards won't prevent state-level criminals from receiving the funds.<ref name=bbccompliance />

In July 2025, the [[European Central Bank]] restricted Revolut's European arm's business activities due to deficiencies in the company's approval processes. ECB ordered Revolut to commission an independent risk review and  review staffing levels, expertise and independence within its product approval process.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.amlintelligence.com/2026/06/latest-ecb-blocked-new-revolut-products-over-compliance-concerns/ |title=ECB blocked new Revolut products over compliance concerns |author=Paul O'Donoghie |date=10 June 2026 |publisher=AML Intelligence |accessdate=15 June 2026}}</ref> Such regulatory measures limited the bank's ability to launch new products. As of June 2026, it was unclear if bank followed the ECB's ruling and the restrictions were lifted.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sifted.eu/articles/european-authorities-curb-revolut |title=Revolut product blitz curbed by European authorities |author=Damisola Sulaiman |date=10 June 2026 |publisher=sifted |accessdate=15 June 2026}}</ref>

On a different occasion, Revolut was blamed for overcompliance, as it froze accounts of its customers with Russian passports and legal residence in Europe in 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cbn.com.cy/article/121965/over-compliance-is-quietly-undermining-the-rule-of-law |title=Over-compliance is quietly undermining the Rule of Law |author=Athanasios Papandropoulos |date=27 November 2025 |publisher=Cuprus Business News |accessdate=15 June 2026}}</ref> Storonsky blamed regulatory pressure. However, legal experts agreed that EU sanctions don't prohibit servicing European residents of Russian origin.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ft.com/content/9f499f4d-f78b-4154-aa2e-cabe9bd22d16 |title=How Russia weaponised global banking to silence dissidents |author=Alexandra Prokopenko |date=1 February 2026 |publisher=Financial Times |accessdate=15 June 2026}}</ref>

=== Alleged Russian connections ===

Following Revolut's incorporation in Lithuania, the company faced allegations of ties to the Russian authorities. [[Stasys Jakeliūnas]], who served as the head of the Lithuanian parliament’s budget and finance committee, stated concerns that the father of Revolut's CEO Storonsky was a top manager of a state-owned [[Gazprom]] and that one company's shareholders [[DST Global]] was connected to Russia via its founder [[Yuri Milner]]. Lithuanian media reported that the company's servers may be potentially moved to Russia, further fueling the controversy. The bank initially made a false statement about Storonsky's lack of family connections with Russia, but later confirmed it.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.imd.org/research-knowledge/finance/articles/revolut-could-allegations-of-russian-involvement-sidetrack-a-fintech-revolution/ |title=Revolut: Could allegations of Russian involvement sidetrack a fintech revolution? |author=Arturo Bris, Gerda Zigiene |date=March 2019 |publisher=International Institute for Management Development |accessdate=15 June 2026}}</ref>

In 2022, Storonsky claimed that he opposes the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian invasion of Ukraine]]. The company offered relocation supports for its Ukraine-based staff.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/johnhyatt/2022/03/01/revoluts-russian-anti-war-billionaire-founder-promises-to-match-donations-to-red-cross-ukraine/ |title=Russian-Born Billionaire Behind Revolut Fintech App Publishes Anti-War Letter |author=John Hyatt |date=1 March 2022 |publisher=Forbes |accessdate=15 June 2026}}</ref> Storonsky renounced his Russian citizenship in October of that year.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rferl.org/a/billionaire-revolut-storonsky-renounces-russia-citizenship/32108805.html |title=Billionaire Revolut Chief Storonsky Reportedly Renounces Russian Citizenship |date=31 October 2022 |publisher=RadioFreeEurope / Radio Liberty |accessdate=15 June 2026}}</ref>

Times]] |date=8 February 2020 |archive-date=2020-02-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200223003235/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/monzo-and-revolut-customer-complaints-are-mounting-at-digital-banks-p9fm3xjmj |url-status=live }}</ref>

In February 2020, ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'' reported that Revolut suspended an account containing £90,000 for more than two months<ref name=telegraph_20000125>{{cite news |last1=Hunt |first1=Marianna |title=Revolut could face lawsuit from customers locked out of their accounts |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/money/consumer-affairs/revolut-could-face-lawsuit-customers-locked-accounts/ |access-date=2020-02-23 |work=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=25 January 2000 |archive-date=2020-02-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200225062025/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/money/consumer-affairs/revolut-could-face-lawsuit-customers-locked-accounts/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and that another customer travelled 500 miles from [[Auvergne]] in France to Revolut's London offices in an unsuccessful attempt to recover £15,000 in an account that Revolut had frozen with no justification given.<ref name="EU">{{cite news |last1=Hunt |first1=Marianna |title=Ex-UCL lecturer forced to travel to London from France in attempts to unblock digital bank account |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2020/01/24/ex-ucl-lecturer-forced-travel-london-france-attempts-unblock/ |access-date=2020-02-27 |work=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=24 January 2020 |archive-date=2020-03-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200306172211/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2020/01/24/ex-ucl-lecturer-forced-travel-london-france-attempts-unblock/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The account was later closed and the money in it returned to the customer's other bank accounts.<ref name="EU"/>

Also in February 2020, ''[[The Times]]'' reported that Revolut suspended and later closed a business account containing €300,000 belonging to Priorité Energie, an energy transition start-up company, preventing the company from paying its staff.<ref name="NS">{{cite news |last1=Dunkley |first1=Emma |title=Nikolay Storonsky's Revolut freezes accounts in money-laundering bungle |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/nikolay-storonskys-revolut-freezes-accounts-in-money-laundering-bungle-5nt3lv6zk |url-access=subscription|access-date=2020-02-23 |work=[[The Times]] |date=23 February 2020 |archive-date=2021-01-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210111020824/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/nikolay-storonskys-revolut-freezes-accounts-in-money-laundering-bungle-5nt3lv6zk |url-status=live}}</ref> Revolut publicly apologised and eventually rectified the problem.<ref name="NS"/>

===UK fraud victims===
In 2023, Revolut reported a 35% reduction in [[authorised push payment fraud]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 October 2023 |title=Revolut doubles financial crime headcount since 2021 to combat fraud |url=https://www.rte.ie/news/business/2023/1031/1413840-revolut-doubles-financial-crime-headcount-since-2021/ |website=rte.ie|access-date=2026-05-31}}</ref> However, the company remained one of the most frequently named financial institutions in UK fraud complaints, prompting scrutiny of its security measures.<ref>{{Cite web |title='I lost £165k to fraud in an hour' – customers say they were let down by Revolut |date=14 October 2024 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cj6epzxdd77o |publisher=BBC|access-date=2026-05-31}}</ref> The number of complaints of fraud reported to [[Action Fraud]], the UK reporting centre for fraud and cybercrime, by Revolut customers rose from 567 in February 2023 to 1,086 for February 2024.<ref name=theguardian_2024apr10_im/>

Prior to Revolut having a banking licence, complaints were made by defrauded Revolut customers to the [[Financial Ombudsman]], which in some cases required Revolut to reimburse and compensate victims, and remove [[Cifas#Fraud databases|fraud markers]] wrongly placed against the individuals.<ref name="org_4189491">{{Cite report |url=https://www.financial-ombudsman.org.uk/decision/DRN-4189491.pdf |title=Decision Reference DRN-4189491 |date=12 July 2023 |publisher=Financial Ombudsman Service|access-date=2026-05-31}}</ref>

Action Fraud received 10,000 reports of fraud naming Revolut in 2023, 2,000 more than [[Barclays]], one of the UK's largest banks, and twice as many as a competitor bank of similar size to Revolut. That year over 3,500 complaints about Revolut were made to the [[Financial Ombudsman Service|ombudsman]], more than any other financial institution. Consumer organisation [[Which?]] did not recommend banking large sums of money with Revolut, saying "They have a track record of not reimbursing people who fall victim to fraud or find themselves in this incredibly difficult situation, [and] of money being taken from accounts even after scam activity has been reported."<ref name="fraud">{{Cite news |date=14 October 2024 |title=Revolut customers say e-money firm failed them after being scammed |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cj6epzxdd77o |work=[[Panorama (British TV programme)|BBC Panorama]]|access-date=2026-05-31}}</ref>

== Partnerships ==
In January 2025, [[Manchester City W.F.C.]] announced Revolut as the training sleeve kit sponsor. This partnership was later extended to include the back-of-shirt sponsors of both the [[Manchester City F.C.|men's]] and women's teams.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Saleh |first=Tariq |date=16 January 2025 |title=Revolut expands into women’s soccer with Man City deal |url=https://www.sportcal.com/news/revolut-expands-into-womens-soccer-with-man-city-deal/ |access-date=28 August 2025 |website=Sportcal |language=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=13 February 2026 |title=City announce Revolut as official back of shirt partner  |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/club/revolut-back-of-shirt-partner-63906575?utm_source=x&utm_medium=organic_social |access-date=13 February 2026 |website=Manchester City |language=}}</ref>

That same month, Revolut became an official partner of the French rugby club [[Stade Toulousain]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Carp |first=Sam |date=2025-08-28 |title=What’s driving Revolut’s global sports sponsorship push? |url=https://www.sportspro.com/insights/analysis/revolut-sports-sponsorship-audi-f1-nba-man-city-cmo-interview/ |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=SportsPro |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In July 2025, [[Audi in Formula One|Audi F1 Team]] announced a multi-year deal with Revolut to be the title sponsor of the team, beginning with the 2026 season.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Baldwin |first=Alan |date=30 July 2025 |title=Revolut to become title partner of Audi F1 team |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/revolut-become-title-partner-audi-f1-team-2025-07-30/ |access-date=30 July 2025 |work=[[Reuters]] |language=}}</ref> In the same month, Revolut was named the Official Global Banking and FX Partner for the Italian football club Como 1907.<ref name=":0" />

In March 2026, Revolut became official back of shirt partner of [[Manchester City F.C.]], extending the relationship with the club to the men's team. <ref>{{Cite web |last=Editorial |first=Man City |title=City announce Revolut as official back of shirt partner |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/club/City%20announce%20Revolut%20as%20official%20back%20of%20shirt%20partner |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=Manchester City FC |language=en}}</ref>

The company also has partnerships in other sports, such as an ongoing agreement with the NBA to serve as an associate partner for the NBA Paris Game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-01 |title=Revolut teams up with NBA to launch co-branded payment cards for basketball fans |url=https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/106181/revolut-teams-up-with-nba-to-launch-co-branded-payment-cards-for-basketball-fans |access-date=2026-03-10 |website=Finextra Research |language=en}}</ref>

Beyond sports, Revolut announced a strategic partnership with [[Wizz Air]] in March 2025 to integrate Revolut Pay as a primary payment method for the airline.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wizz Air partners with Revolut for one-click payments |url=https://thepaypers.com/payments/news/wizz-air-partners-with-revolut-for-one-click-payments |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=thepaypers.com |language=en}}</ref>

On 3 June 2025, Revolut signed a membership agreement with European Payments Initiative (EPI). The agreement includes integration of Wero, mobile-first wallet and instant account-to-account payment solution, into Revolut.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://epicompany.eu/media-insights/revolut-joins-the-european-payments-initiative-to-bring-wero-to-millions-of-new-customers-this-summer-2|title=EPI Company | Revolut joins the European Payments Initiative to bring…|website=epicompany.eu}}</ref>

== Workplace policy ==
In June 2026, Revolut announced that graduate employees and interns joining the company in 2027 would be required to work from the office at least three days a week, marking a retreat from its fully remote policy. The company said the change was intended to support in-person collaboration and mentoring but its remote policy would remain unchanged for other employees.<ref>{{cite news |date=26 June 2026 |title=Revolut scraps 'remote-first' working for graduate hires |url=https://www.ft.com/content/f0e12920-bac5-4f5b-aad1-79e350742d84 |access-date=9 July 2026 |work=Financial Times}}</ref>
